overview: Kenya is a country in East Africa, on the Indian Ocean. Its capital and largest city is Nairobi. Kenya became independent from the United Kingdom in 1963. Swahili and English are its official languages. Kenya is famous for wildlife safaris and for its long-distance runners, who have won many Olympic medals.

geography.text: Kenya rises from a coastal strip on the Indian Ocean to high plateaus in the centre and west, split by the Great Rift Valley. Mount Kenya, the second-highest mountain in Africa, stands close to the equator. The north is dry and semi-desert, while the south-west borders Lake Victoria and includes the Maasai Mara, famous for its great wildebeest migration.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Hot on the coast, mild in the highlands around Nairobi.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Lions, elephants, rhinos and the great migration in the Maasai Mara.

history.text: Some of the oldest human fossils have been found in Kenya. Swahili city-states grew up on the coast and traded across the Indian Ocean. Britain colonised Kenya in the 1890s and took fertile land for white settlers. The Mau Mau uprising of the 1950s was brutally put down, and Kenya became independent in 1963 under Jomo Kenyatta.

events.title: Nobel Peace Prize
events.text: Wangari Maathai wins for her tree-planting movement.

government.text: Kenya is a presidential republic with 47 counties. Its 2010 constitution limits the President to two five-year terms. Elections have sometimes been followed by violence, as in 2007–08. In 2024 youth-led protests forced the government to withdraw tax increases.

economy.text: Kenya has East Africa's largest economy. It exports tea, flowers and coffee, and tourism, especially safaris, is important. Kenya is a leader in mobile money: M-Pesa, launched in 2007, lets people pay with their phones.

culture.text: Kenya has more than 40 ethnic groups, and Swahili and English are official. The Maasai Mara's great wildebeest migration is one of the world's great wildlife spectacles. Wangari Maathai won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2004.

items.title: Great Migration
items.text: About 1.5 million wildebeest cross the Mara River each year.

items.title: M-Pesa
items.text: Mobile money used by most adults.

items.title: Lamu
items.text: A Swahili town listed by UNESCO.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Ugali, a maize porridge, with sukuma wiki (greens) and nyama choma (grilled meat).

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Maasai coming-of-age ceremonies include jumping dances.

sport.text: Kenya is famous for distance running. Eliud Kipchoge became the first person to run a marathon in under two hours in 2019 and won Olympic gold twice. Faith Kipyegon is a three-time Olympic 1,500 m champion. Kenya's rugby sevens team is also strong.

didYouKnow: Kenya's Lake Turkana is the world's largest permanent desert lake.
M-Pesa, launched in Kenya in 2007, was one of the first mobile money services.
